sections.h2: Which Mason County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Three offices in Shelton share the work. The Mason County Treasurer collects the money, the Assessor sets the value, and the Board of Equalization hears appeals. All three use North Fifth Street addresses, and the shared county number is 360-427-9670. Belfair callers can use 360-275-4467 for the Treasurer.

The Treasurer sits on the second floor of Building 1, 411 N 5th Street, open 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays except legal holidays. A drive-up drop box is in the alley. Mail goes to the Mason County Treasurer's Office, PO Box 429, Shelton, WA 98584-0429. Extension 475 reaches the Treasurer and extension 491 reaches the Assessor. The county runs an online tax search called TaxSifter, and the Treasurer takes Visa, MasterCard, Discover and American Express in person, online or by phone through Point N Pay, with a convenience fee under RCW 36.29.190.

sections.h2: What is Mason County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Mason County is a Puget Sound and Olympic foothills county with exactly one incorporated city, Shelton, which is also the county seat. It was cut from Thurston County on March 13, 1854, first called Sawamish County, and took its present name in 1864 for Charles H. Mason, the first Secretary of Washington Territory. The county holds about 959 square miles of land and 92 square miles of water, and part of Olympic National Park and Olympic National Forest lies inside it.

Most residents live outside Shelton in unincorporated places such as Belfair, Allyn, Grapeview, Hoodsport, Skokomish and Union. U.S. 101 and state routes 3, 106 and 108 are the main highways. Census QuickFacts describe the owners who hold these parcels:

  • Population estimate for July 1, 2025: 71,165, up 8.3% since April 2020.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate, 2020-2024: 82.3%, the highest of the four counties in this series.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $411,800.
  • Median household income: $83,270.
  • Residents aged 65 and over: 25.8%.
  • Mean travel time to work: 36.1 minutes.
  • Building permits in 2025: 204.

sections.h2: When are Mason County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The first half is due April 30 and the second half is due October 31, and the Treasurer counts a payment as timely only if it is postmarked by the due date. For 2026, the Treasurer's news release said first-half payments were due Thursday, April 30, with delinquent charges starting Friday, May 1. The release also warned that postmarks through the Postal Service can be delayed and urged owners to mail early.

The deadlines come from RCW 84.56.020. Under the statute, a home with four or fewer units accrues nine percent annual interest on delinquent tax with no penalty. Other property accrues twelve percent plus a 3% penalty on June 1 and an 8% penalty on December 1. The county also notes that an owner with a DNR fire patrol assessment on more than one Mason County parcel may qualify for a refund from the state Department of Natural Resources, and refund requests are due by December 31, 2026.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Mason County assessment?
sections.html:
File an appeal with the Mason County Board of Equalization by July 1 of the assessment year or within 30 days of the date on the Assessor's Notice of Change of Value, whichever is later. Mason County follows the 30-day rule in RCW 84.40.038. Mail the form to the Board of Equalization at 411 N 5th Street, Shelton, WA 98584-3466, or ask the clerk at 360-427-9670 extension 268 to send blank forms.

Timing in 2026 was unusual. The Assessor dated its real property notices September 11, 2026, and the last day to appeal them was October 12, 2026, which has passed. The next notices will carry their own deadline, so read the date on the notice itself.

The Board was established under chapter 84.48 RCW and is independent of the Assessor. It has three members and two alternates who serve staggered three-year terms, and members cannot be elected officials or employees of one. It also hears appeals when the Assessor denies a senior citizen exemption. The county posts forms for real property, personal property, current use, senior exemption review, late filing exceptions and requests to reconvene the Board.

sections.h2: Which relief programs matter when you sell in Mason County?
sections.html:
The Assessor lists five programs, and two of them come with repayment at sale. Taxpayers who qualify can use:

  • The senior citizen and disabled persons exemption, for owners at least 61 years old, retired because of a disability, or a qualifying veteran.
  • A deferral for owners 60 or older, or retired for disability, where the state pays the tax and the deferred amount accrues 5% simple interest.
  • A limited-income deferral of the second half installment, for owners with five years in the home, with applications due September 1.
  • A grant for the widow or widower of a veteran.
  • Current use classification for open space, farm and agricultural land, and designated forest land.

Both deferrals must be repaid when the home is sold, the owner dies or the home stops being the primary residence. That means the deferred tax and interest come due at your closing, so ask the Assessor for the balance before you list. The exemption itself does not carry that repayment.

ESSB 6162 takes effect with the 2027 tax year. According to the Assessor, it raises the income thresholds, gives a full exemption from the state school levy, and lowers the veteran disability rating needed from 80% to 40%. The county lists a $70,000 combined disposable income limit for the 2027 tax year, and renewals are required every three years. The statute is RCW 84.36.381.

sections.h2: What changes when current use land sells in Mason County?
sections.html:
Parcels in the current use program carry a reduced assessment because they are used as open space, farm land or forest land. The application fee is $600 per parcel, and it is nonrefundable. For designated forest land, a timber management plan is required with the first application and again when the property is conveyed or sold.

That last requirement affects a seller. If you hold forest land in Mason County, ask the Assessor what the buyer must file before the deed is signed. The Mason Conservation District offers technical and financial help to landowners, and the DNR's Find Your Forester tool is listed on the county page.

sections.h2: What if Mason County taxes are already behind?
sections.html:
Contact the Treasurer's Foreclosure Deputy at 360-427-9670 extension 485 before the parcel reaches a tax judgment sale. The county publishes a foreclosure information sheet, a minimum bid sheet, public notices of judgment sales, and a link to Bid4Assets, the online auction site.

The Treasurer points owners to three outside resources. The Washington Homeownership Resource Center, at 1-877-894-4663, gives free referrals. A nonprofit counseling agency, American Financial Solutions, is listed. The Assessor's Office can also tell you whether the senior or deferral programs apply to a home with back taxes. Under RCW 84.56.020, the treasurer may set up payment agreements for past due years, and an income-qualified owner living in the home can have interest and penalties waived shortly before the three-year mark when a foreclosure action is pending.

sections.h2: What excise tax does a Mason County seller pay?
sections.html:
The seller usually pays Washington's real estate excise tax, and if the seller does not, the buyer becomes responsible and an unpaid tax can become a lien. It is due on the date of sale, and the deed, affidavit and payment go to the county treasurer. Late payment after one month adds interest at 6% for 2026 and 2027, from the date of sale.

For sales starting January 1, 2027, the Department of Revenue sets the state rate at 1.1% up to $551,000, 1.28% to $1,551,000, 2.75% to $3,051,000 and 3.0% above. The local rate is added to that. Call the Treasurer for the local rate and any deed-recording steps.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Mason County property tax in person?
faqs.a: Pay at the Treasurer's Office, 411 N 5th Street, Building 1, second floor, in Shelton. Hours are 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays, and a drive-up drop box is in the alley.

faqs.q: What is the Mason County deadline to appeal my value?
faqs.a: File by July 1 or within 30 days of the date on your Notice of Change of Value, whichever is later. The 2026 deadline was October 12, 2026, and it has passed.

faqs.q: Do I have to repay a Mason County property tax deferral when I sell?
faqs.a: Yes. Deferred tax and interest come due when the home is sold, the owner dies or the home is no longer the primary residence. Ask the Assessor for the balance before you list.

faqs.q: Who handles tax foreclosure in Mason County?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's Foreclosure Deputy handles it at 360-427-9670 extension 485. The county's foreclosure page links to the minimum bid sheet and the Bid4Assets auction site.

faqs.q: Can I pay Mason County property tax by card?
faqs.a: Yes. The Treasurer accepts Visa, MasterCard, Discover and American Express in person, online or by phone, and a convenience fee applies to every card payment.
